newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sends eight to firing squad in drugs trial.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sends eight to firing squad in drugs trial.

text.p: Vietnam's communist authorities demonstrated public determination to tackle a growing heroin scourge on Wednesday as a court in Hanoi sentenced eight people to death at the end of a dramatic two-week drugs trial.
Hundreds of people gathered outside the People's Court in the city centre as verdicts were read out in a case involving state security officials which has gripped the country for days.

In addition to the death sentences, eight people were given life terms in prison and six others received terms from a suspended sentence to 20 years in jail -- all for involvement in a trafficking ring which is said to have flooded Vietnam with hundreds of kilos of heroin.
"The quick investigation, early trial...and harsh punishment has shown the Vietnamese government's determination not to compromise in the fight against drugs," said a foreign ministry official.
"...at the same time it also shows the strictness and justice of Vietnamese law," she added.

The trial is the biggest yet and most sensational to have surfaced in Vietnam. Half of those convicted were members of Vietnam's powerful security establishment, a body held in fear by some and once considered by many as untouchable.
Two police captains, including lead defendant Vu Xuan Truong, and a senior border guard were among those sentenced to face the firing squad.
"I will go to hell before you," Truong told police officers escorting him. "But I'll reserve places there for you."
Foreign journalists were not allowed to attend the trial, but sources inside said the lead defendants remained expressionless as their sentences were read out.

Truong had said earlier he was resigned to death and on Monday asked the judge for an early execution. His brother and wife, also on trial, were spared the death penalty but received jail terms of life and 20 years respectively.

The case erupted last year following the arrest and conviction of a Laotian drugs trafficker, who broke down shortly before he was due to be executed by firing squad and offered to exchange information on the syndicate in exchange for leniency.
Under Vietnamese law people sentenced to death are given a 15-day appeal period. If the appeal fails, their ultimate hopes lie with a presidential pardon.

While the trial may have been used to demonstrate official toughness it has also highlighted Vietnam's growing role as a market and transit route for drugs from Asia's notorious Golden Triangle region.
Drug experts say the country's moves in recent years to open borders long closed to the outside world, combined with rampant corruption, has brought a bonanza for international dealers.

State newspapers have said a further 20 people were likely to be charged following the trial, but court officials said on Wednesday a new investigation would examine the activities of two Interior Ministry colonels who were witnesses at the trial.
